title: The End of an Era
author: harscoat
relevanceReason: 命中 1 个 AI/科技关键词。
summaryRaw: We knew this day would come.

Some of us have known for decades, have been writing and pontificating about this since Ken Jennings lost at Jeopardy and Kasparov lost at chess. The writing was on the wall, and now the writing is everywhere. Literally. Artificial Intelligence is writing about as well as humans — at least well enough to cause confusion and speculation — and that’s creating an existential crisis among authors, confusion among readers, and legal action within the industry.

When talking about my success as a writer, I almost always bring up the lucky timing I experienced. I finished writing my first novel in 2009, just two years after Amazon released the Kindle. By the time I went to find an agent and publisher, the self-pubbing world of KDP, CreateSpace, and ACX were beginning their inevitable pull. That was dumb luck, and without it I would have written for love but likely never for a living.

This morning, an equally profound thought occurred to me: My lifelong dream of writing novels somehow overlapped with the 20 good years where stories could be published cheaply but not written cheaply. The writing was still hard. The publishing no longer was. I could sweat my way through a manuscript, and then use amazing tools like InDesign and Photoshop to create files, then upload those files FOR FREE to KDP and CreateSpace and hold a book.
Sales and marketing, of course, were always and will always be a different story.

comments.author: inigyou
comments.textRawHtml:
LLMs are writing as well as humans for people who think writing words is the goal. Printing presses also write words better than humans. LLMs are solving the problem one layer higher than printing presses, but still several layers down from the top.

Note that LLMs aren't useless, since they have other strengths which can make them equal or better than humans in certain applications. For instance, they can tirelessly review code for silly mistakes, making them useful in cybersecurity.
comments.textZhHtml:
对于那些认为写作是目标的人来说，法学硕士就像人类一样写作。印刷机也比人类写得更好。法学硕士正在解决比印刷机高一层的问题，但仍然比顶部低几层。

请注意，法学硕士并非无用，因为它们具有其他优势，可以使它们在某些应用中等于或优于人类。例如，他们可以不知疲倦地检查代码中是否存在愚蠢的错误，从而使它们在网络安全中发挥作用。

children.author: bsenftner
children.textRawHtml: Finally, someone else understands that writing is not the goal, the entire point of all of this is our communications between one another and this market for narrative stories is a nice departure and it does convey important knowledge and moral lessons that larger society needs. But it is an indirection, an indirection to the mission of communicating solutions to how to live as a human and that is why we care, why the interest persists despite lifetimes of narrative dreck. We are adrift without instructions, and no religions are not the instructions.
children.textZhHtml: 最后，有人明白写作不是目标，所有这一切的全部意义在于我们彼此之间的交流，而这个叙事故事市场是一个很好的出发点，它确实传达了更大社会需要的重要知识和道德教训。但这是一种间接的方式，是对传达如何作为人类生活的解决方案这一使命的间接方式，这就是我们关心的原因，为什么尽管叙述了一生的废话，人们的兴趣仍然存在。我们在没有指示的情况下随波逐流，没有宗教不是指示。

children.author: docfort
children.textRawHtml: I think the first goal of writing is to talk to yourself. Without an external, unchanging scratchpad, most people cannot keep their thoughts truly straight. It can feel otherwise, but trying to write something about any tricky topic even a few pages in length can take a long time to be self-consistent. Clarifying it takes even longer, especially when you intend to share it. Writing as thinking is definitely a thing. I believe it’s the trickiest part of understanding how such interesting things pop out of a language model trained to predict the next token and rewarded with pleasing sequences. Since it is not thinking, it proves that certain sentences (most?) can be generated thoughtlessly.
children.textZhHtml: 我认为写作的首要目标是与自己对话。如果没有外部的、不变的便签本，大多数人就无法真正保持思路清晰。可能感觉并非如此，但是尝试写一些关于任何棘手主题的东西，即使是几页的长度，也可能需要很长时间才能保持自洽。澄清它需要更长的时间，尤其是当你打算分享它时。写作作为思考绝对是一回事。我相信这是理解如何从经过训练来预测下一个标记并以令人愉悦的序列作为奖励的语言模型中弹出如此有趣的事物的最棘手的部分。既然不是思考，那就证明某些句子（大部分？）可以不假思索地生成。

children.author: foobarian
children.textRawHtml: I like the term I've seen someone use for LLMs: a "thought partner."  Truly it's the duck programming duck I've always wanted.
children.textZhHtml: 我喜欢我看到有人用的 LLM 一词：“思想伙伴”。  确实，这就是我一直想要的鸭子编程鸭子。

children.author: Brian_K_White
children.textRawHtml:
I say that LLM's are a pacifier. LLM output is to conscious output as a silicone nipple is to a breast.

Sure, at some level, there are some people who at least some times, cannot pecieve a difference. That does not prove that there is no difference or that the difference doesn't matter.
children.textZhHtml:
我说LLM是一个安抚奶嘴。 LLM 输出与意识输出的关系就像硅胶奶嘴与乳房的关系一样。

当然，在某种程度上，有些人至少在某些时候无法察觉到差异。这并不能证明没有差异或者差异不重要。

children.author: WorldMaker
children.textRawHtml:
I think that LLM's are a broken mirror or maybe disco ball. What you get back is almost always a reflection of what you put in, just garbled through and with the reflections of so many other people. The best parts that I often get back are mostly just the stuff that I already put in it.

I think that's also where LLMs get the most dangerous. That ELIZA effect of telling you exactly what you told it but in a slightly rephrased way makes you think that you think that your ideas are genius. You've got someone "actively listening" and telling you whatever idea you just gave it was the best idea it ever heard.

That's not what you want from a serious writing partner. You want a writing partner to challenge you, to point out your mistakes and flaws, to make you better, to offer a truly different perspective to your own. You don't want a dark reflection from a "yes man" to spiral into.
children.textZhHtml:
我认为法学硕士是一面破碎的镜子或者迪斯科球。你得到的几乎总是你输入的内容的反映，只是乱码和许多其他人的反映。我经常得到的最好的部分大多只是我已经放入其中的东西。

我认为这也是法学硕士最危险的地方。 ELIZA 的效果是准确地告诉你你所说的内容，但以稍微改写的方式让你认为你认为你的想法是天才的。有人“积极倾听”并告诉你，无论你刚刚提出什么想法，它都是它听过的最好的想法。

这不是你想要从认真的写作伙伴那里得到的。你需要一个写作伙伴来挑战你，指出你的错误和缺陷，让你变得更好，为你提供真正不同的观点。你不想让“唯唯诺诺的人”陷入黑暗。

children.author: foobarian
children.textRawHtml: I think it is a net positive for me, because I am super unconfident by nature and the agreeable, almost sycophantic output from major LLMs give me just enough of a boost to debias me.  They are certainly better than a physical rubber duck.
children.textZhHtml: 我认为这对我来说是一个积极的因素，因为我本质上非常不自信，而主要法学硕士令人愉快的、几乎是阿谀奉承的输出给了我足够的动力来消除我的偏见。  它们肯定比实体橡皮鸭更好。

children.author: visarga
children.textRawHtml: Don't just focus on the model, half the turns in a session belong to the human, it's an instrument that depends on how well the user wields it. It does not need to produce the novel insights, just to support the user to have them.
children.textZhHtml: 不要只关注模型，会话中一半的回合属于人类，它是一种工具，取决于用户如何运用它。它不需要产生新颖的见解，只需支持用户拥有它们即可。

children.author: miki123211
children.textRawHtml:
No.

I think narrative stories are a "brain hack", in the same way heavily processed food, drugs, clickbait, soap operas and TikTok are brain hacks, combined with some exclusivity status signaling games. They're just old enough to have gained a cultural cachet that more modern forms of entertainment don't yet have. Same for art, music, comedy and culture generally.

There is nothing wrong with those "brain hacks", if they make us happy and don't have negative consequences, why not use them, but we should recognize that it's what they are.

I think that an alien intelligence could communicate with us about Ohm's law and Rieman's last theorem, maybe even debate resource and power allocation strategies (democracy, monarchy, capitalism, socialism) with us, they could probably understand the pull of sports, even if they couldn't participate in it themselves, but art and humor would be completely lost on them and considered a weird human excentricity.
children.textZhHtml:
不。

我认为叙事故事是一种“大脑黑客”，就像精加工食品、毒品、点击诱饵、肥皂剧和 TikTok 都是大脑黑客，再加上一些排他性状态信号游戏。他们的年龄已经足够大，已经获得了更现代的娱乐形式尚不具备的文化声望。对于艺术、音乐、喜剧和文化来说也是如此。

那些“大脑黑客”没有什么问题，如果它们让我们快乐并且不会产生负面后果，为什么不使用它们，但我们应该认识到它们是什么。

我认为外星智能可以与我们交流欧姆定律和黎曼最后定理，甚至可能与我们辩论资源和权力分配策略（民主、君主制、资本主义、社会主义）我们，即使他们自己不能参与其中，他们也可能能够理解体育运动的吸引力，但艺术和幽默对他们来说完全不适用，并被认为是一种奇怪的人类怪癖。

children.author: nicf
children.textRawHtml: This sounds like a fully general argument against being alive and having experiences; you could equally well call love a "brain hack". I also care a lot about solving practical problems, but the reason it's important to solve them is because it leads to human flourishing, which includes participating in all these activities you're deriding. Otherwise why are we doing anything at all?
children.textZhHtml: 这听起来像是一个反对活着和拥有经验的完全普遍的论点；你同样可以将爱情称为“大脑黑客”。我也非常关心解决实际问题，但解决这些问题之所以重要是因为它会带来人类的繁荣，其中包括参与所有你嘲笑的这些活动。否则我们为什么要做任何事情？

children.textZhHtml: 目的是尽你所能缴纳税款、利息、租金和各种贡品，并在接到命令时为统治者的利益牺牲自己的生命。

children.author: tauroid
children.textRawHtml:
The "story form" is a brain hack, i.e. a way of disseminating "problem X may cause Y and be resolved by Z". Whether that's useful depends entirely on what's being communicated and how.

Art, music, humour, poetry are more basic and the commonality is more or less "I bring you surprising phenomena". If phenomena are surprising to you then your mental model of the world needs improving.

What's Riemann's last theorem?
children.textZhHtml:
“故事形式”是一种大脑黑客，即一种传播“问题X可能导致Y并由Z解决”的方式。这是否有用完全取决于所传达的内容和方式。

艺术、音乐、幽默、诗歌是更基础的，共性或多或少是“我给你带来了令人惊讶的现象”。如果现象令您感到惊讶，那么您的世界思维模型需要改进。

黎曼最后定理是什么？

children.author: bsenftner
children.textRawHtml: I understand where you are coming from, that brain hack is how we remember cause and effect. It's very much like the use of Jazz Hands to signal to the dullards "now is the moment you're supposed to remember and say 'oh, I liked that'" A narrative story used as a vehicle to convey moral lessons and life guidance is the Jazz Hands of our fragmented and incomplete human instruction manuals.
children.textZhHtml: 我明白你的想法，大脑黑客就是我们记住因果关系的方式。这很像使用“爵士手”向笨蛋发出信号“现在是你应该记住并说‘哦，我喜欢那个’的时刻”。作为传达道德教训和生活指导的载体的叙事故事就是我们支离破碎且不完整的人类指导手册中的“爵士手”。

children.author: tavavex
children.textRawHtml:
Culture and art can teach something to its audience, unlike most of the garbage you likened it to. It's clear you don't hold it in much regard, since you compare it to outright scams (clickbait) and even imply that consuming fiction is basically done for virtue signalling.

But like it or not, humans are not computers. They are animals with messy, complex thinking and reasoning that is impossible to fully describe, and incredibly complex societal systems created from their chaotic interactions. These messy people don't learn from datasheets and reference manuals, even if you'd like it to be otherwise.

Of course, there's a place for non-fiction, I like some of it a lot. But art has subtlety to it - instead of smacking people in the face with data and lists of objective measurements, it can pry into them by using the human ability to imagine themselves in other shoes, experience emotions that aren't results of real life events, and much more. There is a reason why parents teach their children values by reading them fables or educational stories, not the legal code of their jurisdiction. And this is also why fiction actually changes the minds of people reading it, arguably doing it more effectively than nonfiction. Slop (clickbait, average tiktok content, whatever else you're imagining) doesn't make you feel new things or think of something you haven't thought of before, art does.

The aiens are also a bit of a copout. You're just assuming that there's bound to be this perfect species (that are effectively computers) that operate only on mathematics and discrete logic, who are obviously superior to us and can show us our wrong ways. What if computers aren't always superior? Or what if organic life requires some of that messiness you don't like to be viable? What if the aliens had their own weird things we could never relate to?
children.textZhHtml:
文化和艺术可以向观众传授一些东西，不像你所比喻的大多数垃圾。很明显，你不太重视它，因为你将其与彻头彻尾的骗局（点击诱饵）进行比较，甚至暗示消费小说基本上是为了传递美德信号。

但不管你喜欢与否，人类不是计算机。它们是具有无法完全描述的凌乱、复杂的思维和推理的动物，以及由它们混乱的相互作用创建的极其复杂的社会系统。这些混乱的人不会从数据表和参考手册中学习，即使您希望不是这样。

当然，非小说类作品也有一席之地，我非常喜欢其中的一些。但艺术也有它的微妙之处——它不是用数据和客观测量列表来打人们的脸，而是通过利用人类想象自己换位思考的能力来窥探它们，体验非现实生活事件结果的情感等等。父母通过阅读寓言或教育故事而不是其管辖范围内的法律来教导孩子价值观是有原因的。这也是为什么小说实际上改变了阅读它的人的思想，可以说比非小说更有效。 Slop（点击诱饵、普通的抖音内容，无论你想象的其他什么）不会让你感受到新事物或想到你以前没有想到过的东西，艺术却可​​以。

人工智能也有点逃避现实。你只是假设一定存在这种完美的物种（实际上是计算机），它们仅在数学和离散逻辑上运行，它们显然比我们优越，并且可以向我们展示错误的方法。如果计算机并不总是那么优越怎么办？或者，如果有机生命需要一些你不喜欢的混乱才能生存怎么办？如果外星人有他们自己的奇怪的东西我们永远无法联系怎么办？

这样做的目的是什么？你没有不同意，你只是偏离了方向。这又是一次“大脑黑客”吗？如果是这样，他们就有问题了。他们经常使词语看起来像是某种东西，但实际上并非如此。

children.author: underlipton
children.textRawHtml:
We already suspect that many non-human animals have a "sense of beauty" and a sense of humor. At least one other species spontaneously dances on the "beat" to music (parrots).

I think alien intelligence would be able to appreciate art and humor, even without necessarily feeling it viscerally, as we do. We know that our particular brands of them rely on highly-developed and specific aspects of our psychology, but at a basic level, they seem to fundamentally be about congruence, incongruence, expectation, and interpretation/perspective. Any embodied intelligence that can observe physical reality is capable of grokking those concepts.
children.textZhHtml:
我们已经怀疑许多非人类动物具有“美感”和幽默感。至少还有一个物种会自发地随着音乐的“节拍”跳舞（鹦鹉）。

我认为外星智慧生物能够欣赏艺术和幽默，即使不一定像我们一样发自内心地感受到它。我们知道，我们的特定品牌依赖于我们心理学的高度发展和特定方面，但在基本层面上，它们似乎从根本上是关于一致性、不一致、期望和解释/观点。任何能够观察物理现实的实体智能都能够理解这些概念。
